US military will livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:14:41 UTC
15:14:41 KST

Convicted military base shooter Nidal Hasan's execution will take place on 3 December at Fort Hood military base, where he committed the shooting. It will be the first US military execution carried out by a firing squad since World War II.
The firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, the Pentagon said Thursday, a controversial revelation about plans for the first military execution by firing squad since World War II after Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth had described it as being "public."
The UN promptly condemned the US decision as "torture".
"The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture," said the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights.
The UN body said it had made similar statements about public executions in Afghanistan and Iran, saying they "constitute a form of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment".
Nidal Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist, shot and killed 13 people and injured 32 others at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009.
"We are going to make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public", this is how US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the "public" execution of convicted military base shooter Nidal Hasan.
"People need to understand that... there's serious consequences for these types of things", said Hegseth.
His execution by firing squad will be livestreamed on 3 December; it will be the first execution by the US military in more than 65 years, and the first carried out by firing squad since World War II.
"I kind of like the mentality we had in World War II, which was win, which was understand when the enemy attacks you, you need to stand your ground", Hegseth said.
Officials in the Pentagon clarified Thursday that the execution would be livestreamed and that more details would follow.
The revelation from Hegseth about the public nature of the execution has raised further questions about how the death penalty is carried out in the US, especially after the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee.
'We'll see him on December 3'
"He is going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be", said Hegseth.
In an interview with right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec, the Pentagon chief was asked if Hasan had made any final request. "Don't care. We'll see him on December 3", Hegseth said — the day Hasan is slated to die.
Hasan could choose to resist execution and file a habeas petition — a legal request to review the legality of a detention — in civilian court, which could significantly delay the execution, experts said.
"It frankly might outlast the current administration, and who knows if the next one will have the same penchant for executions", said Eugene R. Fidell, a visiting lecturer at Yale Law School specialising in military law.
Deborah Denno, a death penalty expert and law professor at Fordham University, said livestreaming an execution could make the process "much more transparent" and inform the public about all that capital punishment entails.
Those are benefits that she said would be useful at a time when Pike’s botched execution has raised fresh questions about the manner by which criminal defendants are put to death for their crimes. "I think it could possibly be a good idea because it would be transparent and the public would be fully aware that it’s happening", she said.
Firing squad 'less inhumane'
When many states have had difficulty carrying out lethal injections due to difficulty accessing drugs or finding medical professionals willing to participate in executions, firing squads are coming to be seen as a less inhumane alternative, said Brenner Fissell, a professor at Villanova Law and vice president of the National Institute of Military Justice.
"Firing squads can be a quicker, cleaner, more precise way to execute a prisoner", he said. "I don’t think that’s what’s motivating this. There’s a perceived masculinity and military-ness to firing squads that is part of the aura Hegseth is trying to emphasise — the 'lethality culture".
Elisabeth Semel, co-director of the Death Penalty Clinic at UC Berkeley Law, said Hegseth’s announcement raises a host of legal and public policy questions, including concerns for the dignity of the defendant, who will be eligible to view the execution and what the Trump administration has in mind in opting for an unusual spectacle.
Though there has been a long-running discussion about the idea of televising an execution, "I don’t recall a situation in which it was instigated by the government. I think that also raises serious questions about what the motivation of the government is", she said.
"This is a president who’s about spectacle and that’s, I think, precisely the message that he intends to deliver", Semel said, adding that she was sceptical that the administration had given a second thought to the legal and social questions being presented by the decision.
Media reports state that Trump, who approved Hasan’s execution, has previously been critical of public executions in Iran, at times using the possibility of protesters being killed by the Iranian government as a possible rationale for military action that preceded his ultimate choice to attack Iran on 28 February.
US executions scrutinised after failed injection
Texas has carried out the first execution in the US since Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived a failed lethal injection last week. Jamaal Howard, 46, has received a lethal injection on Wednesday evening and was shortly after declared dead.
Lawyers for Howard asked to pause the execution in spite of Pike's botched lethal injection last week, but the courts denied the request.
A further two executions are scheduled to take place in November — death row inmates John Rubio and Reinaldo Dennes.
Since the beginning of the year, the US has executed 30 people. In 2025, US executions reached the highest figure since 2009, with 47 people being put to death.

World Post Day 2026: history of the holiday and interesting facts
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
09:13:02 EEST
15:13:02 KST

World Post Day 2026: history of the holiday and interesting facts
Kyiv • UNN
World Post Day is observed on October 9, established following the creation of the General Postal Union in 1874. In Ukraine, during the war, the postal service provides logistics, humanitarian deliveries, and communication with millions of people.
Every year on October 9, the world celebrates World Post Day — a holiday honoring one of humanity’s most important inventions. For centuries, the postal service has remained a convenient means of communication between people, cities, and continents. Today, it is not merely the delivery of paper letters but a global logistics network that supports international trade and connects millions of people. UNN will рассказывать about the history of this day, the postal service in Ukraine, and interesting facts
Why World Post Day is celebrated on October 9
The date of October 9 was not chosen by chance. On this day in 1874, during an international congress in Bern, Switzerland, representatives of 22 countries signed the Treaty of Bern. This document established the General Postal Union, which was renamed the Universal Postal Union in 1878.
Previously, each state established its own tariffs, rules, and formatting requirements, which necessitated the conclusion of hundreds of bilateral agreements. Delivering a letter between continents was extraordinarily expensive and took months because of endless customs and bureaucratic procedures. The Treaty of Bern united countries into a single postal system with standardized tariffs. This became a genuine information revolution of the 19th century.
The official decision to celebrate World Post Day annually on October 9 was adopted in 1969 at the 14th UPU Congress in Tokyo. Since then, this day has symbolized unity and international cooperation.
How the postal service has changed
Just a few decades ago, the primary task of postal workers was sending paper letters, holiday cards, and periodicals. People waited weeks for letters, and keeping in touch with relatives abroad required patience.
With the advent of the internet, traditional handwritten letters gave way to email and messengers. However, this did not destroy the postal industry but led to its large-scale transformation. The rapid development of e-commerce turned postal operators into logistics companies. Parcels and goods from online stores became the primary items delivered.
Modern postal services are high-tech operations. Traditional branches are supplemented by networks of 24-hour parcel lockers, mobile apps for real-time shipment tracking, artificial intelligence for route optimization, and automated sorting lines that process thousands of packages per hour.
How the Ukrainian postal service operates during the war
Under conditions of full-scale war, Ukraine’s postal system — both the state-owned "Ukrposhta" and private operators, including "Nova Poshta" — has demonstrated remarkable resilience and become an important element of national security.
An important factor in the development of Ukrainian postal logistics has been its international network. Nova Poshta’s entry into the European market during the war. The company opened its own branches under the Nova Post brand in many European countries — Poland, Germany, the Czech Republic, Romania, Lithuania, Italy, Spain, France, and many others. This enabled millions of Ukrainians abroad to easily and quickly send and receive parcels from home, maintaining contact with their relatives.
In addition, Ukrainian operators built a powerful humanitarian logistics network, delivering medicines and military equipment free of charge. Despite the closure of civilian air connections, Ukrposhta, together with international partners, established alternative ground and air routes through European countries, preserving export opportunities for Ukrainian businesses.
On April 12, 2022, Ukrposhta issued the legendary postage stamp "Russian warship, go f... yourself!". The idea of creating the stamp arose after the brave response of a Ukrainian border guard from Snake Island to the Russian cruiser’s demand that he surrender. A competition for the best design received more than 1,700 entries from artists around the world, and the winner was Ukrainian illustrator Borys Groh.
The first print run of the stamp amounted to 1 million copies: 500,000 for domestic mail within Ukraine and 500,000 for international mail. Its release sparked unprecedented excitement and kilometer-long lines outside the Main Post Office in Kyiv. Symbolically, already the day after the stamp was issued, on April 13, the same Russian flagship "Moskva" was struck by Ukrainian Neptune missiles and sank, making the stamp prophetic. Later, on May 23, 2022, Ukrposhta released a second series — "Russian Warship ... DONE!" — in a record print run of 5 million copies. Sales of these stamps and charity auctions raised tens of millions of hryvnias to support the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Interesting Facts About the Postal Service
-  The world's first postage stamp appeared in Great Britain in May 1840 and went down in history under the name "Penny Black." It depicted the profile of Queen Victoria. 
-  The most remote post office is located in Antarctica at Port Lockroy station. Despite the extreme conditions and icy winds, more than 70,000 postcards are sent from there every year to every corner of the planet. 
-  In Canada, Santa Claus has an official postal code — H0H 0H0 — which appears to reproduce his signature "Ho-ho-ho." Every year, postal workers reply to millions of letters from children. 
-  In the 19th and 20th centuries, underground pneumatic mail systems operated in many of the world's major cities, including Paris, Berlin, and New York, where capsules containing letters traveled through tubes propelled by compressed air.

Okinawa lawmakers seek review of Japan-US military pact after Marine accused of murder
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:09:32 UTC
15:09:32 KST

Japan’s Okinawa prefectural assembly has called for a “fundamental review” of the Japan-US Status of Forces Agreement after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in a case that has sparked protests and public outrage.
The assembly adopted a resolution on Friday urging the US military to take action against Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who has denied wrongdoing, to “prevent a recurrence”, Kyodo News Agency reported.
It also adopted a statement addressed to the Japanese government, with both documents calling for a fundamental review of the agreement governing US forces stationed in Japan.
Ballard, assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Ginowan, was arrested on Sunday and sent to prosecutors. He is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in the prefectural capital of Naha on Saturday.
Okinawa hosts roughly half of the 50,000 US troops stationed in Japan, making the island a focal point of longstanding opposition to the US military presence.
Protests and military response
The case has triggered protests in Okinawa and Tokyo, with demonstrators calling for action against the accused and renewed scrutiny of the US military’s conduct.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has condemned the incident. The Japanese government has summoned the US ambassador and the commander of US forces in Okinawa to lodge protests.
The US military in Okinawa imposed a 48-hour pause in operations from Wednesday and announced a curfew for the next 30 days, beginning on Friday.
Okinawa was under US control from 1945 to 1972 and has repeatedly seen protests following cases of sexual assault involving US military personnel.
“Past crimes involving US military personnel, including those against women and girls, have angered residents of Okinawa,” the report said.

Schools in several Malaysian states as well as its federal and administrative capitals will be closed on Friday, the education ministry said, after smoky haze caused by forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia pushed air pollution to unhealthy levels.
The areas affected include the states of Johor, Malacca, Negeri Sembilan and Selangor on the Malaysian peninsula, as well as the country's capital Kuala Lumpur and its administrative centre Putrajaya, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said in a Facebook post late on Thursday.
Schools will also be closed in the Rompin district of Pahang state, she said.
"I have asked all state education departments and district education offices to continue to monitor the haze situation and take immediate action if the situation requires it," she said.
Malaysia's Air Pollutant Index classifies air quality as "unhealthy" from 101 to 200, "very unhealthy" from 201 to 300, and "hazardous" above 300. On Friday morning, 37 areas recorded unhealthy API levels, according to government data.
Indonesia has struggled to contain forest and land fires across several provinces which have led to thick haze in neighbouring nations including Malaysia and Singapore.
Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto had agreed to take necessary steps to combat the haze, with Malaysia ready to offer assistance. Anwar said he had asked Malaysia's foreign minister to push for a meeting of ministers from the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN to coordinate a regional response and support Indonesia's efforts.

Nandigram, Rejinagar results to indicate political mood after BJP's rise to power (Representative file photo)
NEW DELHI: BJP’s candidates maintained comfortable leads in Nandigram and Rejinagar as counting continued for the West Bengal assembly bypolls, with the Congress emerging as the runner-up in both constituencies.In Nandigram, BJP candidate Hasirani Rath was leading by 9,600 votes after the first round of counting, while Congress candidate Milan Pradhan was in second place. In Rejinagar, BJP candidate Sakharav Sarkar secured 11,614 votes after the second round, while Congress candidate Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi was trailing with 581 votes.
Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) candidate Gulam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, had polled 446 votes in Rejinagar after the second round, according to trends shown by news channels. The Election Commission had not released official figures confirming the leads at the time of reporting.Counting began at 8 am amid tight security at the counting centres. The bypolls, held on Tuesday, are being watched as an early electoral test of West Bengal’s political landscape following the BJP’s victory in the Assembly elections earlier this year.Nandigram fell vacant after chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who won both Nandigram and Bhabanipur in the assembly elections, retained Bhabanipur.
The BJP fielded Hasirani Rath, the mother of Adhikari’s slain personal assistant, Chandranath Rath, who was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP’s election victory.Rejinagar became vacant after Humayun Kabir retained Naoda, where he had also won. His son, Gulam Nabi Azad, is contesting the bypoll on an AJUP ticket. The results from both seats are being closely watched for an early indication of the BJP’s electoral strength in the state and the opposition’s position amid divisions within the TMC.Nandigram holds political significance for both the BJP and the TMC. The constituency was central to the anti-land acquisition movement that helped bring the TMC to power in 2011. It was also where Suvendu Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee in the 2021 Assembly election. Adhikari, now chief minister, won the seat again in 2026 but retained Bhabanipur, necessitating the bypoll. The BJP fielded Hasirani Rath, whose son Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Adhikari, was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP won the Assembly elections.
The contest in Nandigram has also been shaped by divisions within the TMC. The Mamata Banerjee-led faction’s nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew after meeting Adhikari, following which Banerjee backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan. A rival TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee also contested the seat under a separate temporary party identity and the ‘envelope’ symbol. The result will indicate whether opposition cooperation can translate into votes and how the rival factions fare.More details awaited.

Ukraine's Foreign Trade Deficit Approached $40 Billion in First Eight Months of 2026
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
09:08:04 EEST
15:08:04 KST

Ukraine's foreign trade in goods in January–August 2026 was characterized by imports significantly exceeding exports and the concentration of the negative trade balance in relations with several of its largest partners. According to calculations based on the table “Ukraine's Foreign Trade with Selected Countries” as of August 31, total trade turnover amounted to $92.95 billion, imports to $66.25 billion, and exports to $26.70 billion. The negative balance reached $39.55 billion, while imports exceeded exports by a factor of 2.48.
Exports covered only 40.3% of the value of imported goods. China was the largest individual trading partner and supplier, Poland was the main market for Ukrainian products, and the European Union as a whole accounted for 59.1% of Ukraine's merchandise exports. Meanwhile, the largest positive trade balances were recorded in trade with Moldova, Spain, and Egypt.
“For every hundred dollars of merchandise imports, there were approximately forty dollars of merchandise exports. This ratio demonstrates the limited ability of the export sector to balance the economy's demand for foreign products. Some imports support production and reconstruction, so they must be assessed with regard to the purpose of the goods. To improve the balance in the long term, the equipment purchased must help increase the output of competitive products in Ukraine,” said Maksym Urakin, PhD in Economics and founder of the Experts Club information and analytical center.
Total Trade Volume and Largest Partners
Ukraine recorded its largest trade turnover with China at $20.56 billion, or 22.1% of the total. Poland ranked second with $9.54 billion, followed by Germany with $6.10 billion. Ukraine had almost the same volume of trade with Turkey, at $6.08 billion, with the difference compared with Germany amounting to just $20.9 million. The United States completed the top five partners with $3.91 billion.
These five countries accounted for 49.7% of trade turnover, while the ten largest partners accounted for 63.4%. Thus, trade results with a relatively small group of countries largely determined Ukraine's overall foreign trade balance.
Ukraine's Ten Largest Trading Partners by Trade Turnover in January–August 2026, USD Billion
Source: State Customs Service of Ukraine
The next largest partners included Romania, with trade turnover of $2.05 billion, Spain with $1.98 billion, Lithuania with $1.80 billion, France with $1.77 billion, and Greece with $1.52 billion. Total trade turnover with the 27 EU member states amounted to $43.60 billion, or 46.9% of the overall figure. Ukrainian exports to the EU totaled $15.78 billion, imports reached $27.81 billion, and the deficit amounted to $12.03 billion.
The EU's high share of exports means that access to the European market is of decisive importance for Ukrainian producers. At the same time, substantial purchases from EU countries constitute a separate source of the trade deficit. The situation within this trade relationship is uneven: the largest gaps are recorded with Poland and Germany, while Ukraine has positive trade balances with Spain and the Netherlands.
Imports and Dependence on Major Suppliers
China supplied $19.64 billion worth of imports, or 29.6% of total merchandise imports. Supplies from Poland amounted to $6.28 billion, or 9.5%, while those from Germany reached $4.38 billion, or 6.6%. Together, these three countries accounted for 45.7% of Ukraine's merchandise imports.
The five largest suppliers also included Turkey with $3.99 billion and the United States with $3.21 billion. The combined share of the top five reached 56.6%, while the ten largest suppliers accounted for 68.3%. Other major sources of imports included Italy with $1.83 billion, the Czech Republic with $1.67 billion, Hungary with $1.55 billion, and Slovakia and Lithuania with approximately $1.34 billion each.
The State Customs Service provides a breakdown of the overall commodity structure for the same period. In January–August 2026, Ukraine imported machinery, equipment, and transport vehicles worth more than $29.9 billion, fuel and energy products worth more than $9.5 billion, and chemical industry products worth more than $9 billion. These categories accounted for more than 73% of imports; machinery, equipment, and transport represented approximately 45%. [2]
This ratio indicates the significant role of industrial and energy products in imports. However, the broad category of machinery and transport includes goods intended for different purposes. Its entire value cannot be interpreted as investment in production: doing so would require separate analysis of industrial equipment, components, vehicles, and final consumer goods.
“The concentration of almost one-third of imports with a single supplier makes Ukrainian businesses sensitive to supply conditions from China. Logistics disruptions or changes in component prices may affect many enterprises simultaneously. At the same time, reducing purchases without affordable alternatives could constrain Ukrainian production itself. The practical task is to diversify suppliers and develop domestic production of goods for which Ukraine has the economic and technological prerequisites,” Urakin commented.
Exports and the Geography of Sales Markets
Poland remained the largest export market, receiving goods worth $3.26 billion, or 12.2% of Ukraine's total exports. Turkey ranked second with $2.09 billion and a share of 7.8%, followed by Germany with $1.73 billion and 6.5%. Italy followed with $1.52 billion, the Netherlands with $1.31 billion, and Spain with $1.29 billion.
Exports to China amounted to $924.2 million, Romania to $878.0 million, Hungary to $845.6 million, and Slovakia to $792.4 million. Egypt and Moldova purchased Ukrainian goods worth $751.0 million and $750.5 million, respectively. Supplies to the Czech Republic amounted to $705.2 million, while exports to the United States reached $700.0 million.
Exports were less concentrated among individual countries than imports: the three largest markets accounted for 26.5% of shipments, the top five for 37.1%, and the top ten for 54.8%. At the same time, the EU's dominance as a combined market means that the diversity of destination countries only partially reduces dependence on the economic and regulatory conditions they share.
According to the State Customs Service, food exports exceeded $15.4 billion over the eight months, exports of metals and metal products approached $2.7 billion, and exports of machinery, equipment, and transport approached $2.4 billion. The approximate shares of these groups in total exports were 58%, 10%, and 9%, respectively. Food products remained the main source of merchandise export revenue. [2]
“The geography of exports allows Ukraine to operate in different markets, but the commodity structure remains heavily dependent on food products. For such shipments, harvest volumes, global prices, and transportation costs are particularly important. The development of processing can increase revenue per unit of raw material, although it requires investment and a stable energy supply. At the same time, industrial exports must be expanded so that the performance of several agricultural commodity groups has less influence on the overall picture,” Maksym Urakin noted.
Negative Trade Balance and Concentration of the Deficit
The largest bilateral deficit was recorded in trade with China at $18.71 billion. This was equivalent to 47.3% of Ukraine's net merchandise trade deficit. Exports to China covered only 4.7% of imports from that country, while Chinese goods accounted for 95.5% of bilateral trade turnover.
The second-largest deficit was recorded with Poland at $3.02 billion. Germany followed with $2.65 billion, the United States with $2.51 billion, and Turkey with $1.90 billion. Together, the negative trade balance with these five countries amounted to $28.79 billion.
Significant deficits were also recorded in trade with Greece at $1.07 billion, the Czech Republic at $964.7 million, Lithuania at $864.6 million, France at $864.5 million, and Taiwan at $844.5 million. Thus, the imbalance extended far beyond relations with the single largest supplier.
The sum of negative trade balances across all deficit-producing trade relationships reached $43.90 billion. Positive balances totaling $4.35 billion in other rows of the table reduced this amount to an overall deficit of $39.55 billion. Accordingly, China accounted for 42.6% of the sum of bilateral deficits, while the five largest deficit-producing trade relationships accounted for 65.6%. This provides a more accurate picture of their concentration than comparing them solely with the net result after surpluses are taken into account.
“The deficit with China exceeds the combined negative trade balance with all EU countries. This illustrates how unevenly Ukraine's dependence on imports is distributed. At the same time, a bilateral deficit in itself does not determine whether trade with a particular country is economically beneficial. It is necessary to assess how imported goods are used domestically and what contribution they make to employment, production, and future exports,” Urakin emphasized.
Positive Trade Balance and Markets Dominated by Ukrainian Supplies
Ukraine recorded its largest positive trade balance with Moldova at $640.6 million. With exports of $750.5 million, imports from that country amounted to $109.9 million, meaning that Ukrainian supplies exceeded imports by almost 6.8 times. Spain ranked second in terms of the surplus, at $613.0 million: exports to Spain reached $1.29 billion, while imports amounted to $681.8 million.
The third-largest surplus was recorded with Egypt at $493.5 million. Algeria followed with $361.0 million, Lebanon with $258.7 million, and Libya with $219.8 million. The positive balance with Iraq amounted to $169.1 million, the Netherlands to $160.1 million, Tunisia to $157.0 million, and Yemen to $134.0 million.
The five largest surpluses – with Moldova, Spain, Egypt, Algeria, and Lebanon – totaled $2.37 billion, or 54.4% of all positive balances. However, surplus-generating trade relationships offset only 9.9% of the sum of bilateral deficits overall. Even successful export markets had not yet generated sufficient revenue to balance purchases from the largest suppliers.
“Moldova, Spain, and Egypt demonstrate that Ukraine has markets where its own supplies significantly exceed imports. These should be considered a basis for expanding product ranges and strengthening long-term relationships with buyers. However, a large surplus in an individual trade relationship does not necessarily mean it can be increased rapidly without demand constraints. To have a tangible impact on the overall balance, exports must increase simultaneously across many markets,” Maksym Urakin believes.
Commodity Structure of Trade with Selected Countries
A detailed breakdown by commodity helps explain differences between trade relationships. Below, figures for January–August 2026 are supplemented with reference data for 2025 and other explicitly specified periods. Historical shares describe their respective periods and cannot automatically be applied to the first eight months of 2026.
According to GMK Center calculations based on State Customs Service data, Ukraine supplied 7 million tonnes of iron ore to China in January–August 2026, 38% less than a year earlier. This represented approximately 44% of Ukraine's total iron ore exports by physical volume during the period, which amounted to 15.8 million tonnes. The Chinese market thus remained extremely important for the mining industry, although Ukraine's total exports to China were much smaller than imports.
For its part, the National Institute for Strategic Studies noted in its review of 2025 that machinery, equipment, and transport accounted for 69.8% of Ukrainian imports from China. Comparing these data from different periods highlights the differences in the commodity profiles of bilateral trade: the major role of manufactured products in Chinese supplies is combined with the importance of raw materials in Ukrainian exports. The precise structure of this exchange during the first eight months of 2026 can only be determined through a complete breakdown of commodity categories.
In January–August 2026, Ukraine shipped 2.1 million tonnes of iron ore to Poland. For comparison, Slovakia received 2.9 million tonnes over the same period. These figures illustrate the role of both markets in sales of products from Ukraine's mining industry.
A broader Polish commodity profile is contained in the Polish Ministry of Development and Technology's response to parliamentary inquiry No. 17426, reproduced in the Politoskop database. According to the GUS data for 2025 cited there, major supplies from Ukraine to Poland included soybean oil worth €399.7 million, iron ores and concentrates worth €342.3 million, and rolled ferrous metal products worth €315.5 million. In the opposite direction, substantial volumes consisted of petroleum products worth €1.76 billion, unmanned aerial vehicles worth €759.6 million, and passenger cars worth €555.8 million. These figures come from Polish statistics for the full year 2025 and therefore serve as a separate description of the commodity composition of trade.
According to preliminary German official agricultural statistics for 2025, industrial goods accounted for approximately 94% of German supplies to Ukraine. Meanwhile, Germany imported agricultural and food products from Ukraine worth approximately €1.3 billion and industrial sector goods worth €1.8 billion. Agricultural supplies notably included oilseeds, primarily rapeseed, as well as vegetable oils worth €172 million and processed fruit products and preserved fruit worth €101 million. This structure indicates that Ukrainian exports to Germany also include a substantial industrial component.
According to the analysis by the National Institute for Strategic Studies, corn was an important item in Ukrainian exports to Turkey in 2025, with shipments worth approximately $1.2 billion. Among imports from Turkey, petroleum products accounted for $639 million, while the aggregated category of “other goods” amounted to $2.1 billion. Without further detail, it would be incorrect to associate the latter with any specific industry. Data for January–August 2026 also confirm the presence of metallurgical trade: according to GMK Center calculations, Ukraine exported 83,200 tonnes of pig iron to Turkey.
In January–August 2026, the United States purchased 900,600 tonnes of Ukrainian pig iron, while total exports of this product amounted to approximately 1.03 million tonnes. Thus, the US market accounted for approximately 87% of shipments by physical volume. Italy received 26,500 tonnes during the same period. Sales of an individual commodity may be much more concentrated in one market than Ukraine's total exports across countries.
Data from the Verkhovna Rada Committee on Agrarian and Land Policy, citing the State Customs Service, demonstrate the importance of the Spanish, Italian, and Indian markets for the vegetable oil industry. In the first half of 2025, Spain purchased Ukrainian sunflower oil worth $356.9 million, Italy purchased $337.5 million, and India purchased $326.1 million. Their shares in the value of exports of this product were 12.88%, 12.18%, and 11.77%, respectively. This is an example of the specialization of individual markets in sales of Ukrainian processed agricultural products, not an estimate of their shares for January–August 2026.
Economic Implications and Conditions for Improving the Balance
The geographic and commodity data indicate a combination of high demand for imported industrial products with exports dominated by food products, while ore and metallurgical products play a substantial role in certain trade relationships. Given this structure, opportunities to improve the balance depend on production capacity, energy supply, accessible logistics, and conditions for entering foreign markets.
At the same time, the merchandise trade deficit is not equivalent to a deficit in the overall balance of payments or an automatic reduction in foreign exchange reserves by the same amount. External financing is also influenced by trade in services, income, transfers, and financial transactions. Therefore, the figure of $39.55 billion specifically characterizes the gap between merchandise exports and imports within the statistics presented.
“Improving the trade balance requires expanding the capacity of Ukrainian enterprises to produce goods and sell them abroad. Equipment purchases can contribute to this if they are accompanied by investment in production, access to energy, and clear operating conditions. Stable transportation and the ability to fulfill contracts without forced interruptions are equally important for exporters. It is the growth of competitive domestic production that can gradually narrow the gap between imports and exports,” Maksym Urakin concluded.

Black Sea Attacks Raise Risks for Bulgaria's Economy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:08:00 UTC
15:08:00 KST

Bulgaria is not facing a major economic shock at present, but growing risks to Black Sea trade and business could affect the economy, politician and economist Kuzman Iliev and Mikhail Krastev, Executive Director of the Union for Economic Initiative, said on NOVA NEWS.
Their comments followed attacks on two vessels inside Bulgaria’s Exclusive Economic Zone in the Black Sea.
Iliev said Bulgaria was only beginning to understand the economic risks created by the war and military activity in the Black Sea. "We Bulgarians are currently like someone going to boxing training for the first time - clutching their face and saying, 'I got hit.'" He added, "The Black Sea has been a war zone for quite some time; we didn't realize it, but now we must acknowledge it - purely from an economic standpoint as well,"
Iliev said the ports of Varna and Burgas were among Bulgaria’s main economic arteries, handling about 20 million tons of goods each year. He warned that additional disruptions to commercial shipping caused by risks in the Black Sea could have serious effects on the Bulgarian economy.
One immediate consequence, according to Iliev, could involve insurance costs. If insurers classify the Black Sea as a high-risk war zone, companies could face higher expenses, which could then push up the prices of goods and services. "Since August, we have seen insurance premiums double," Iliev said.
He stressed that greater risk does not mean future developments can necessarily be predicted, but businesses need to prepare for different possible scenarios.
Krastev said maritime trade in the Black Sea remains possible, although operating conditions have become considerably more dangerous.
"Since the start of the war in Ukraine, over 200 ships have been hit. Far fewer have sunk. The Black Sea is a war zone, and security is insufficient," he said.
Krastev also said the military conflict was already affecting the European economy, with the industrial sector among those influenced by political decisions and sanctions imposed against Russia.
Iliev identified another potential risk, saying international companies could start bypassing Bulgarian ports and redirecting their trade through other countries. He said Bulgaria should therefore put greater emphasis on expanding its railway network and highways so that alternative transport routes are available if maritime traffic becomes restricted.

TRNC slams EU for preserving 'unjust status quo' over Turkish Cypriot isolation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:06:58 UTC
15:06:58 KST

The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) on Thursday criticised the European Union after the European Commission referred to past commitments to end the isolation of Turkish Cypriots and efforts to “build bridges” and “enhance dialogue,” which the TRNC dismissed as an attempt to create a “false impression” of progress.
The TRNC Foreign Ministry said the references in the Commission’s letter did not reflect the realities on the island, accusing the EU of maintaining a “biased and insincere” stance on the Cyprus issue.
The ministry said Turkish Cypriots had for years been forced to live under what it described as inhumane isolation and embargoes in violation of international law and human rights.
It said restrictions in areas ranging from education and sports to culture and economic life violated the fundamental rights of Turkish Cypriots.
The statement also accused the EU of seeking to preserve the “unjust status quo” on the island and of yielding to vetoes by the Greek Cypriot side.
“There is an obvious reality: the people of the TRNC are still being subjected to inhumane isolation before the eyes of the EU and the international community,” the statement said.
EU shows ‘no willingness’ to ease isolation
The TRNC statement described the European Commission’s references to 2004 European Council decisions aimed at ending the isolation of Turkish Cypriots, as well as its claims about “building bridges” and “enhancing dialogue,” as “nothing more than an attempt to create a false impression.”
“The EU has taken no concrete steps, and has demonstrated no sincere approach, political will or vision, to eliminate the unjust restrictions imposed on the Turkish Cypriot people and the inhumane obstacles created by the Greek Cypriot side.
"The EU, which supports the Greek Cypriot leadership that even prevents our young people and athletes from establishing ties with the world, is the biggest protector of the status quo on the island," it added.
“We cannot take seriously the European Union and its so-called representative, (European Commission Vice President and EU Special Representative for Cyprus) Raffaele Fitto, which disregard the will, sovereign equality, and equal international status of the Turkish Cypriot people and distort the realities on the island through biased reports, letters and statements.”
The statement said the Turkish Cypriot people and the TRNC will continue their struggle under their own state structure, with the strong support of the Republic of Türkiye, and will remain determined to defend their rights on the basis of sovereign equality despite all embargoes and attempts at obstruction.
“The TRNC will not accept these empty, delaying tactics and approaches aimed at concealing the existing injustice on the island. There is one fundamental truth that the international community must understand: unless these outdated embargoes imposed on the Turkish Cypriot people are completely lifted, and our sovereign equality and equal international status are recognised, the EU’s declarations of ‘goodwill’ will have no validity in our eyes.
“At the same time, it is impossible to understand the portrayal in the press and public of a false impression that positive developments are taking place within the EU regarding the isolation. Far from taking steps to lift the isolation of Turkish Cypriots, the EU will show no willingness even to ease it.”
Decades-long problem
The island has been mired in a decades-long dispute between Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots.
In 1974, a Greek Cypriot coup aimed at Greece’s annexation of the island led to Türkiye’s military intervention as a guarantor power to protect Turkish Cypriots from persecution and violence. As a result, the TRNC was founded in 1983.
It has seen an on-and-off peace process in recent years, including a failed 2017 initiative in Switzerland under the auspices of guarantor countries Türkiye, Greece and the UK.
The Greek-administered Southern Cyprus entered the EU in 2004, the same year Greek Cypriots single-handedly blocked a UN plan to end the longstanding dispute.

Coalition, opposition tie at 52 seats as Netanyahu's Likud gets closer to Eisenkot's Yashar - poll
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:06:50 UTC
15:06:50 KST

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party gained one seat this week, bringing the coalition bloc into a tie with the opposition bloc at 52 seats each, according to a Maariv poll released Friday, amid memorial events and protests marking the third anniversary of the October 7 massacre.
The opposition bloc lost one seat after Yair Golan's Democrats dropped by one mandate, while the other parties in the bloc remained unchanged. Within the coalition, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party lost one seat, while the Religious Zionist Party gained one. The Arab parties maintained their combined strength of 12 seats.
Respondents were asked, "If elections to the Knesset were held today, which party would you vote for?" Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party led the poll with 21 seats, followed closely by Likud with 20 and Naftali Bennett's B'yachad with 13. The Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu each received nine seats, while Otzma Yehudit secured eight.
The Joint Arab List, United Torah Judaism, and Shas each received seven seats, followed by the Religious Zionist Party with six and Ra'am with five. Amcha Yisrael and the Reservists and Economic Party rounded out the list with four seats each.
Opposition voters show greater motivation to vote
The poll found that 78% of respondents were certain they would vote in the upcoming elections, while another 18% said they expected to vote. The remaining 4% indicated they were unlikely to cast a ballot.
Opposition supporters expressed greater motivation to vote, with 86% of those planning to support an opposition party saying they were certain they would cast a ballot, compared with 81% of coalition supporters.
In head-to-head comparisons of candidates' suitability to serve as prime minister, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot maintained his six-percentage-point lead over Netanyahu, receiving 46% support compared with the prime minister's 40%. The gap was unchanged from the previous poll.
Netanyahu, however, narrowed the gap with former prime minister Naftali Bennett to just two percentage points. Bennett received 44% support, compared with 42% for Netanyahu.
The prime minister also held a six-percentage-point lead over Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman, receiving 44% support compared with Liberman's 38%.
Majority oppose Arab party joining next coalition
The poll also found that 59% of Israelis oppose an Arab party joining the governing coalition after the elections, while 36% support such a move and 5% said they did not know.
By contrast, 53% of Israelis support including a haredi (ultra-Orthodox) party in the next governing coalition, while 41% oppose it and 6% said they did not know.
When asked whom they would prefer to serve as prime minister after the elections, 38% of Israelis chose Netanyahu, followed by Eisenkot with 24% and Bennett with 14%. All other candidates received single-digit levels of support.
The poll was conducted on October 7 and 8 among a representative sample of Israeli adults aged 18 and older, including Jewish and Arab respondents.
The poll was conducted by Lazar Research, headed by Dr. Menachem Lazar, in cooperation with Panel4ALL. A total of 4,667 people were invited to participate in the survey, with 700 completing it, matching the initial sample size of 700. The maximum margin of sampling error was 3.7 percentage points.

Putin celebrates birthday with former German chancellor Schröder
Russian leader Vladimir Putin has celebrated his 74th birthday with former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder.

Schröder travelled to Moscow to meet staff and management of the Globus supermarket chain. He has joined the supervisory board of Hyperglobus, which operates Globus-branded hypermarkets in Russia and became independent of German holding company Globus Holding GmbH & Co. KG in 2025.
In Germany, Schröder's new role in Russia has been described as a "betrayal of Europe".
Several German politicians and economists criticised Schröder's appointment to a senior position at the Globus hypermarket chain in Russia.
Background:
- Eighty-two-year-old Gerhard Schröder served as chancellor of Germany from 1998 to 2005 and led the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD) from 1999 to 2004. He has faced years of criticism for his close ties with Russia and his work for Russian energy companies.
- After the full-scale war began, he never distanced himself from the Kremlin. Most recently, in January 2026, the former chancellor spoke in favour of resuming energy cooperation with Russia and called for Russia not to be demonised despite its aggression against Ukraine.

Congressional candidate caught on camera hurling antisemitic insults at Israeli father
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
06:05:44 UTC
15:05:44 KST

A U.S. congressional candidate was arrested on suspicion of committing a hate crime after verbally attacking an Israeli father who was driving his young son to school. Matthew Arndt, the Green Party's candidate in Wisconsin, was filmed calling the father a "fucking traitor" and shouting "Fuck Israel." Arndt himself encouraged the publicity that ultimately led to his arrest. "Post this on social media. I'm running for Congress," he shouted at the father.
The incident occurred Thursday morning in Mequon, a suburb of Milwaukee. The Israeli man's car had a sticker featuring an Israeli flag and the words "Fuck Hamas." The father said Arndt began tailgating him for no apparent reason, overtook his vehicle, rolled down his window and shouted insults about Israel and Jews. Arndt then swerved between lanes in front of him. "Iwasn't sure if he was trying to get me off the road," the Israeli man told a local radio station.
The father photographed Arndt's license plate and followed him to a gas station, where he confronted him and began recording. Arndt also hurled insults at the "Israel lobby," shouted "Free Palestine" and identified himself by name. "You're a great guy. I'm definitely gonna vote for you," the father replied sarcastically. His young son was sitting in the back seat and, according to the father, was becoming increasingly distressed.
The father, who has lived in the United States for about 12 years, said he grew up in a community that lost more than 100 people in the October 7 massacre. He stressed that the sticker was directed at Hamas. "I have nothing against the Palestinians. I definitely have an issue with an organization that wants the Jews dead," he said.
Speaking about the congressional candidate, he added: "The first thought that comes to mind is, even if I disagree with someone, I would never want someone that acts like this to run for Congress."
Arndt, 54, an accountant and investment adviser, claimed the Israeli man had followed and harassed him. He apologized for his behavior but insisted that "the message stands" and that his remarks were directed at Israel, not Jews. "The only mistake I made here is not giving a calmer message," he said.
Police described the congressional candidate's remarks as antisemitic. No charges have yet been filed, but his party condemned his behavior. "Shouting obscenities at someone in a parking lot doesn't advance that cause," the Green Party said.
On his campaign website, Arndt calls for severing ties with Israel and declares that America belongs to Jews and Muslims alike: "Any politics that teaches us to hate each other is not patriotism. It is poison."

Finland should be demanding much more from data centre projects, business promo boss says
Finland
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09
09:04:54 EEST
15:04:54 KST

Finland is giving away its resources to tech giants on far too modest terms, according to Lassi Noponen, CEO of state-owned Business Finland.
"In Sweden, for example, Meta is involved in carbon capture in the Stockholm area, and that's a completely different scale than 'lights for the running track'," Noponen said.
His "lights for the running track" jibe refers to how minor the conditions Finnish municipalities are setting for major companies building data centres — such as Google's promises to build saunas in Muhos and solar panels in Kajaani.
Noponen's opinion carries a good deal of weight. He leads Business Finland, a part of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment, which advises and assists foreign companies wanting to invest in Finland. The outfit is contacted by prospective data centre builders on a daily basis.
Noponen's phone rang while he was speaking with Yle. "That was about a data centre project," he grinned afterwards.
According to Noponen, data centres should be required to make investments of a completely different scale for Finland's benefit, compared to current demands.
Municipalities are currently negotiating with data centre companies, seeking tax revenue and local benefits — but Noponen said this would require coordination at the national level, since municipalities' bargaining power doesn't reach the level he's talking about.
Beyond calls for new electricity production — which Noponen also supports — he sees the electricity connection itself as a lever. Data centres typically receive their grid connection directly from state grid operator Fingrid. A pending law change would let Fingrid prioritise which applicants are first in line to receive scarce new connections.
"Research and development activity, or some other condition, could move a data centre builder higher up the priority list when we grant our limited electricity connection permits."
Tougher terms won't scare firms off
He further noted that companies could also improve their position by sourcing components and services from Finland — leveraging the country's strong power electronics industry, cooling specialists and wide subcontracting base.
Data centre projects do bring work and income to the construction sector and local hotels — but these effects don't last long. In contrast, Noponen's proposed conditions could deliver a broader, longer-lasting boost to Finland's economy.
He said that if Finland plays its cards right, a new 'data economy' could be born.
Throughout the time he spent speaking with Yle, Noponen repeatedly insists that Finland has a strong hand. Data centres are being built worldwide at a staggering financial pace. According to a September report by consultancy firm PwC (PricewaterhouseCoopers), companies are spending more than 700 billion euros on data centre projects this year alone.
"Finland is one of the best places to build because of our natural conditions," Noponen said, pointing to the country's cool climate, available land and electricity access — which PwC's report named as the biggest bottlenecks for data centres around the world.
Noponen doesn't think tougher conditions will scare off international data centre operators.
"I don't believe for a second that international data centre operators' interest in Finland will stop if we require things that build Finland's data economy over a slightly longer timeframe."
So lights for the running track really won't cut it?
"No, it won't."

IN DEPTH: Why are India's 'cockroaches' protesting again?
The Indian capital, New Delhi, has been turned into a fortress with train and metro cancellations, barricades and heavy police presence ahead of Saturday's planned protests against the chief of India's electoral body.
DW's Seerat Chabba explains why the protests are happening again.
Noida airport to be renamed after PM Modi
The recently-built Noida Airport at Jewar will be renamed Narendra Modi International Airport, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced on Friday.
Modi inaugurated the airport near Noida, one of Delhi's satellite cities, on March 28.
"The Council of Ministers of Uttar Pradesh expresses its gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for gifting the state the Noida International Airport at Jewar. The Cabinet has approved a proposal to name it Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar," Adityanath, who belongs to Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), said.
Uttar Pradesh, where the airport is located, is the most populous state in India and is bound for elections next year.
INDIA bloc MPs to meet President Murmu — reports
Leaders from the opposition INDIA bloc are expected to meet President Droupadi Murmu on Friday over their demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, news agencies ANI and PTI reported.
The reported meeting comes after opposition lawmakers, led by Congress' Rahul Gandhi, took to the streets in New Delhi's heart of political powerin daily protests this week.
The protests took place amid a heightened deployment of security personnel and led to Gandhi being briefly detained on two successive days, along with his sister and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, congress workers and other opposition members.
The delegation of opposition leaders is reported to meet Murmu at 8 p.m. local time (1430 UTC).
India slams US Green Card curbs and Vance's 'indentured servants' remark
India's Foreign Ministry said on Friday that steps announced by the United States concerning its Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM) "do not advance shared ambitions" of New Delhi and Washington.
The statement comes after the US suspended eight companies, including India's Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL, from filing for green cards for their foreign workers. (Scroll down our updates to read more on the US move).
Talent mobility is of "tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact," India's Ministry of External Affairs said.
The ministry clarified that the suspension of applications under PERM was distinct from the H-1B visa program.
"The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies," it said.
The ministry also appeared to criticize comments by US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday that described H-1B visa workers as "indentured servants".
"Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," the ministry said.
It added that the "unwarranted" descriptions "ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."
CJP's Dipke calls protest 'fundamental' right
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abijeet Dipke said on Friday that he was poised to go on with the movement's planned protest in New Delhi on October 10, despite being denied permission by the police.
"Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site; Article 19 gives the fundamental right to protest. So, what is the need to get permission?" Dipke told news agency ANI as he declared that the rally would go ahead.
"Did they take permission before deleting 13 crore (130 million) votes? You want that we should not agitate against those who are rigging elections? This cannot be possible. The country cannot run like this. To save the nation, we will protest," he told ANI.
Protesters are calling for India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down over alleged irregularities in voter lists.
Police deny permission for October 10 'Cockroach' protest
Police have not authorized the Cockroach Janta Party's planned demonstrations in New Delhi on Saturday.
The Delhi Police said on Friday that they had received an application from the CJP on October 7 informing them of the protest but it was on "very short notice."
"Our established guidelines require such requests to be submitted 10 days prior to the planned protest, which was not the case here," Joint Commissioner of Delhi Police Nupur Prasad told a press conference.
The official went on to add that CJP's alleged violation of rules during their previous protest was taken into account in denying them permission to protest.
Prasad said that Section 163 of India's criminal procedure law was in force in the New Delhi area, barring any form of assembly or protest.
Over 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in the city ahead the planned protest, according to news agency PTI.
CJP protest: Train services to two Delhi stations to be canceled on October 10, reports say
Indian Railways has canceled mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 a.m. and 2 p.m. on October 10 amid a protest called by the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), Indian media reports said Friday.
The Times of India cited an internal railway order as saying that the decision was made due to "anticipated severe road traffic congestion" around the two major stations in the capital.
Meanwhile, Delhi police have proposed the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations in the capital and reducing train frequency at the stations, news agency ANI reported, citing an official communication.
India's Cockroach movement leaders have been sounding the bugle for a nationwide march to New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 to demand the resignation of the country's top poll official.
India's Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL suspended from US green card filings
In a setback for Indian IT workers, the United States has suspended Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL from its Permanent Labor Certification program.
The certification allows employers to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers.
The Indian companies are on a list of eight major tech firms, including Microsoft, which have been barred from applying for the program under which foreign employees can work permanently in the US.
The Trump administration said an alleged abuse of the program was behind its decision.
"I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini," Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said Thursday.
Sonderling said the suspensions were due to ongoing federal investigations into the companies.
Indian media reports have said that the move could potentially impact thousands of the country's IT professionals.
According to reported figures, Indian applicants secured nearly 70% of all US H-1B visa approvals in the 2025 fiscal year.
News agency ANI on Friday cited a report by the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) as saying that the US green card freeze is a warning for the Indian IT sector to prepare for broader restrictions on foreign workers.
The New Delhi-based think tank advised that Indian IT companies should diversify export markets, strengthen delivery from India and expand local hiring in the US where needed, ANI reported.
It also called for more focus on artificial intelligence to reduce the sector's vulnerability to sudden changes in US policy, according to ANI.
India: Cockroach Janta Party leaders allege mass detentions ahead of Delhi protest, decry 'emergency'
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ramps up its call for a protest march in New Delhi on October 10 over alleged voter roll manipulation, the youth-led movement has accused India's authorities of mass detentions of its members.
CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan and activists from across the country were among those arrested, CJP leaders said in a series of social media posts on Thursday night.
Baliyan was released later in the evening after being arrested by Rajasthan police at his house, CJP Co-Convener Ashutosh Ranka said on X on Friday.
Ranka claimed that at least 10,000 people were detained country-wide on Thursday.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged on X that a group of the movement's volunteers from the state of Telangana were arrested by Madhya Pradesh police onboard a train in Bhopal.
The movement earlier said that a group of students from the western Indian city of Pune who were headed for the planned protest in Delhi were also detained. The CJP said they were being taken on a bus to an unknown location.
There have been no police statements on the alleged detentions so far.
Cockroach movement describes detentions as 'emergency'
Leaders of the CJP have railed against the alleged mass arrests, likening the situation to a "state of emergency."
"Why not just declare EMERGENCY?", Dipke said as he reacted to a video of the students from Pune purportedly being detained.
The last time an emergency decree was issued in India was under former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in the mid-70s. Emergency powers were applied by the Congress leader for 21 months, with civil liberties being suspended, most of the opposition being jailed and media censored.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) calls the period a "dark chapter" in India's history.
Another prominent CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the Modi government of being "at war with its own young citizens."
"Hello India. We are under a State of Emergency," Das wrote on X.
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke set to arrive in Delhi on October 10
Meanwhile, founder 'Cockroach' Dipke has said that he will land in Delhi on Saturday and march to Jantar Mantar.
"This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you," Dipke said.
Thousands are expected to converge at the capital's Jantar Mantar protest site on Saturday to participate in CJP's protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Jantar Mantar served as ground-zero for the viral online Cockroach movement's debut protest in July which culminated with the resignation of the then-education minister.
The CJP, opposition parties and their student units have been holding near-daily demonstrations against Kumar.
Around 130 million names have been removed from electoral rolls under an exercise called Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Opposition leaders and critics say that those struck off the lists include a huge number of minority voters.
They accuse Modi's BJP of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains, questioning the independence of the Election Commission of India (ECI), which is overseeing the exercise.
The ECI and the BJP deny the allegations.

The recently-built Noida Airport at Jewar will be renamed Narendra Modi International Airport, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced on Friday.
Modi inaugurated the airport near Noida, one of Delhi's satellite cities, on March 28.
"The Council of Ministers of Uttar Pradesh expresses its gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for gifting the state the Noida International Airport at Jewar. The Cabinet has approved a proposal to name it Narendra Modi International Airport, Noida-Jewar," Adityanath, who belongs to Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), said.
Uttar Pradesh, where the airport is located, is the most populous state in India and is bound for elections next year.
INDIA bloc MPs to meet President Murmu — reports
Leaders from the opposition INDIA bloc are expected to meet President Droupadi Murmu on Friday over their demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, news agencies ANI and PTI reported.
The reported meeting comes after opposition lawmakers, led by Congress' Rahul Gandhi, took to the streets in New Delhi's heart of political powerin daily protests this week.
The protests took place amid a heightened deployment of security personnel and led to Gandhi being briefly detained on two successive days, along with his sister and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, congress workers and other opposition members.
The delegation of opposition leaders is reported to meet Murmu at 8 p.m. local time (1430 UTC).
India slams US Green Card curbs and Vance's 'indentured servants' remark
India's Foreign Ministry said on Friday that steps announced by the United States concerning its Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM) "do not advance shared ambitions" of New Delhi and Washington.
The statement comes after the US suspended eight companies, including India's Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL, from filing for green cards for their foreign workers. (Scroll down our updates to read more on the US move).
Talent mobility is of "tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact," India's Ministry of External Affairs said.
The ministry clarified that the suspension of applications under PERM was distinct from the H-1B visa program.
"The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies," it said.
The ministry also appeared to criticize comments by US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday that described H-1B visa workers as "indentured servants".
"Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive," the ministry said.
It added that the "unwarranted" descriptions "ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem."
CJP's Dipke calls protest 'fundamental' right
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abijeet Dipke said on Friday that he was poised to go on with the movement's planned protest in New Delhi on October 10, despite being denied permission by the police.
"Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site; Article 19 gives the fundamental right to protest. So, what is the need to get permission?" Dipke told news agency ANI as he declared that the rally would go ahead.
"Did they take permission before deleting 13 crore (130 million) votes? You want that we should not agitate against those who are rigging elections? This cannot be possible. The country cannot run like this. To save the nation, we will protest," he told ANI.
Protesters are calling for India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to step down over alleged irregularities in voter lists.
Police deny permission for October 10 'Cockroach' protest
Police have not authorized the Cockroach Janta Party's planned demonstrations in New Delhi on Saturday.
The Delhi Police said on Friday that they had received an application from the CJP on October 7 informing them of the protest but it was on "very short notice."
"Our established guidelines require such requests to be submitted 10 days prior to the planned protest, which was not the case here," Joint Commissioner of Delhi Police Nupur Prasad told a press conference.
The official went on to add that CJP's alleged violation of rules during their previous protest was taken into account in denying them permission to protest.
Prasad said that Section 163 of India's criminal procedure law was in force in the New Delhi area, barring any form of assembly or protest.
Over 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in the city ahead the planned protest, according to news agency PTI.
CJP protest: Train services to two Delhi stations to be canceled on October 10, reports say
Indian Railways has canceled mail and express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4 a.m. and 2 p.m. on October 10 amid a protest called by the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), Indian media reports said Friday.
The Times of India cited an internal railway order as saying that the decision was made due to "anticipated severe road traffic congestion" around the two major stations in the capital.
Meanwhile, Delhi police have proposed the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 metro stations in the capital and reducing train frequency at the stations, news agency ANI reported, citing an official communication.
India's Cockroach movement leaders have been sounding the bugle for a nationwide march to New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 to demand the resignation of the country's top poll official.
India's Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL suspended from US green card filings
In a setback for Indian IT workers, the United States has suspended Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL from its Permanent Labor Certification program.
The certification allows employers to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers.
The Indian companies are on a list of eight major tech firms, including Microsoft, which have been barred from applying for the program under which foreign employees can work permanently in the US.
The Trump administration said an alleged abuse of the program was behind its decision.
"I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini," Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said Thursday.
Sonderling said the suspensions were due to ongoing federal investigations into the companies.
Indian media reports have said that the move could potentially impact thousands of the country's IT professionals.
According to reported figures, Indian applicants secured nearly 70% of all US H-1B visa approvals in the 2025 fiscal year.
News agency ANI on Friday cited a report by the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) as saying that the US green card freeze is a warning for the Indian IT sector to prepare for broader restrictions on foreign workers.
The New Delhi-based think tank advised that Indian IT companies should diversify export markets, strengthen delivery from India and expand local hiring in the US where needed, ANI reported.
It also called for more focus on artificial intelligence to reduce the sector's vulnerability to sudden changes in US policy, according to ANI.
India: Cockroach Janta Party leaders allege mass detentions ahead of Delhi protest, decry 'emergency'
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ramps up its call for a protest march in New Delhi on October 10 over alleged voter roll manipulation, the youth-led movement has accused India's authorities of mass detentions of its members.
CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan and activists from across the country were among those arrested, CJP leaders said in a series of social media posts on Thursday night.
Baliyan was released later in the evening after being arrested by Rajasthan police at his house, CJP Co-Convener Ashutosh Ranka said on X on Friday.
Ranka claimed that at least 10,000 people were detained country-wide on Thursday.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged on X that a group of the movement's volunteers from the state of Telangana were arrested by Madhya Pradesh police onboard a train in Bhopal.
The movement earlier said that a group of students from the western Indian city of Pune who were headed for the planned protest in Delhi were also detained. The CJP said they were being taken on a bus to an unknown location.
There have been no police statements on the alleged detentions so far.
Cockroach movement describes detentions as 'emergency'
Leaders of the CJP have railed against the alleged mass arrests, likening the situation to a "state of emergency."
"Why not just declare EMERGENCY?", Dipke said as he reacted to a video of the students from Pune purportedly being detained.
The last time an emergency decree was issued in India was under former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in the mid-70s. Emergency powers were applied by the Congress leader for 21 months, with civil liberties being suspended, most of the opposition being jailed and media censored.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) calls the period a "dark chapter" in India's history.
Another prominent CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the Modi government of being "at war with its own young citizens."
"Hello India. We are under a State of Emergency," Das wrote on X.
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke set to arrive in Delhi on October 10
Meanwhile, founder 'Cockroach' Dipke has said that he will land in Delhi on Saturday and march to Jantar Mantar.
"This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you," Dipke said.
Thousands are expected to converge at the capital's Jantar Mantar protest site on Saturday to participate in CJP's protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Jantar Mantar served as ground-zero for the viral online Cockroach movement's debut protest in July which culminated with the resignation of the then-education minister.
The CJP, opposition parties and their student units have been holding near-daily demonstrations against Kumar.
Around 130 million names have been removed from electoral rolls under an exercise called Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Opposition leaders and critics say that those struck off the lists include a huge number of minority voters.
They accuse Modi's BJP of using the exercise as a tool to secure future electoral gains, questioning the independence of the Election Commission of India (ECI), which is overseeing the exercise.
The ECI and the BJP deny the allegations.
Welcome to our coverage
This is Dharvi Vaid Dhulia from DW's studio in New Delhi, bringing you our daily capsule of all the biggest headlines creating a stir in India.
Protests over the deletion of millions of voters from India's electoral rolls have gripped the world's largest democracy.
The bloc of parties opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi — rallied by Modi's main political adversary Rahul Gandhi — has been taking to the streets of the Indian capital since Wednesday. In turn, Gandhi and other opposition lawmakers were briefly detained on two consecutive days.
Now, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement has accused the Indian authorities of mass detentions ahead of their planned protest in New Delhi tomorrow.
Parts of central Delhi remain under heavy security, with reports saying that thousands of additional paramilitary personnel are being deployed to the capital over the protests.
In other news, Indian IT bigwigs Infosys, Tata, Wipro and HCL have found themselves among a list of companies suspended from the United States green card program.

Hong Kong needs tougher inspection regime, experts say after CK Asset building fiasco
Hong Kong lawmakers call for more inspectors and barring of errant contractors from government tenders after serious lapses at Kwun Tong project
Lawmakers and engineering sector leaders have called for a review of Hong Kong’s building inspection mechanism and a blacklist to bar errant contractors from government tenders, after a developer said half of the city’s first privately built “starter homes” project will be demolished due to shoddy steel work.
The government should review the inspection regime and increase its supervisory manpower, lawmakers and engineers said on Friday, calling for inspectors to be stationed at construction sites of privately built subsidised housing estates rather than relying on spot checks.
The call came after the Buildings Department said on Thursday it had approved property developer CK Asset Holding’s plan to tear down and rebuild three of the six blocks at the Anderson Road development in Kwun Tong, with remedial work continuing on the rest.
Earlier investigations found that the steel reinforcement in parts of the towers diverged significantly from approved plans, with fewer reinforcement bars used than required.

Eesti Laul 2027 gets 155 entries from over 20 countries
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-09

Eesti Laul 2027 gets 155 entries from over 20 countries
A total of 155 songs have been submitted to Eesti Laul 2027, Estonia's annual competition to pick its Eurovision Song Contest entry.
The deadline was Thursday lunchtime, and the 155 entries come from more than 20 countries, not only from neighboring ones such as Finland and Latvia, but from further afield too – including from the U.S. and Australia.
Sixty of the songs are in Estonian and 95 in other languages, including one in a made-up language. A "blind" jury of several dozen people will now assess all 155 offerings.
Spokespeople said this year's group of authors stands out for its international reach,.
"Estonian artists and authors are increasingly working across borders," said Eesti Laul producer Riin Vann, who noted a trend for a growing international entrant list, with this year's list of countries being a good example of that.
The broad-based jury of people working in the music business or related fields will now assess the submitted songs. These will be judged blindly, ie. just on the merits of the song, without knowing who the act or songwriter is.
A total of 12 songs will reach the main Eesti Laul final, with the winner to be decided on January 30 at the gala finals concert at the Unibet Arena.
ERR will reveal this year's shortlisted contestants at the end of this month, and the public will get the chance to all these songs at the end of November.
Estonia's Eesti Laul winner last year was Vanilla Ninja with the song "Too Epic To Be True," which did not make it through the Eurovision semi-finals. The semi-finals and grand final this year take place in Burgas, Bulgaria, in mid-May.
